sentences.text: This section extends the remote stand performance concept by describing how border, customs, and apron sensing inputs become constraints in the daily operating plan.
Border release status is represented as a readiness attribute on each affected flight record in the Regional Flow Platform, separate from aircraft readiness and airline commercial readiness.
The Airport Duty Manager produces the Customs Hold Release Note when border processing confirms that a held arrival may proceed to normal turnaround handling.
Customs hold indicators are represented as operational constraints that prevent premature stand release, passenger transfer assumptions, or departure readiness claims.
A flight under a customs hold may remain physically parked and technically serviceable while still being unavailable for normal passenger, baggage, or crew movement decisions.
When border release status is unknown, the Demand Prediction Service treats the turnaround milestone as uncertain rather than assuming that the planned connection interval is valid.
The Airport CDM Portal displays border and customs status in a controlled view so that only authorized operational users see the clearance condition needed for coordination.
The Regional Flow Manager uses aggregated border delay exposure to decide whether an arrival regulation should be adjusted or whether delay absorption should remain local to the airport.
The Airline Operations Coordinator uses customs hold visibility to adjust connection protection, passenger messaging assumptions, and expected aircraft turnaround timing.
The Slot Allocation Engine treats an unresolved customs hold as a reason to avoid assigning an aggressive departure sequence position to the affected flight.
The Arrival Regulation Console uses the Medical Diversion Notice to protect arrival priority, stand assignment timing, and downstream border coordination in the active arrival plan.
Customs status changes are time stamped before they are used in sequencing so that operational decisions are based on the latest authoritative clearance state.
The East Apron Sensor reports stand occupancy transitions, pushback lane blockage durations, and sensor confidence values at a synchronized event time.
West Apron Sensor observations are used to verify whether remote stand areas and service roads are actually available for the traffic pattern shown in the plan.
The Surface Surveillance Adapter normalizes apron sensing data into movement, occupancy, and blockage events that can be correlated with flight milestones.
The Ramp Movement Board presents apron sensor events as operational evidence for stand release, taxi lane availability, and vehicle conflict assessment.
The Gate Conflict Detector uses border status and apron occupancy evidence to distinguish a true gate conflict from a temporary clearance delay.
The Tower Sequence Manager considers confirmed apron blockage when determining whether a departure can be included in the next practical movement sequence.
The Capacity Assessment Module applies persistent apron congestion as a local capacity factor when estimating achievable departure throughput during Normal Operations and Adverse Weather Mode.
The Time Synchronization Service is required because customs status events and apron sensor events must align with Calculated Takeoff Time and Target Off Block Time decisions.
The Business Rules Registry defines which border and customs states block sequencing, which states require human confirmation, and which states are informational only.
The Data Governance Steward maintains the access rules and retention rules for border and customs data because the data can affect both operational outcomes and passenger privacy obligations.
The Alert Distribution Hub issues targeted alerts when a customs hold conflicts with an assigned stand plan or when apron sensing contradicts a declared off-block milestone.
The Collaborative Decision Log records the operational reason when border release status, customs hold status, or apron sensing data changes a sequencing or stand allocation decision.
The Performance Analytics Warehouse compares planned clearance assumptions with actual border release timing and apron availability to improve future demand prediction and resource planning.
